record.notes: Channel Pump Station, 455 Berry St -- an above-grade SFPUC wastewater/stormwater pump station between 6th and 7th Streets, built 1979 and upgraded 2010, with a pumping capacity of 103 million gallons per day (the largest of the city's five combined-sewer pump stations), operating continuously in both dry and wet weather; conveys flows through the Channel force main to the Southeast Treatment Plant. Its distinctive round architectural form (metal I-beam frame, ceramic tile and channel-glass walls under a butterfly roof) was noted in press coverage for its design. Identified by the owner while reviewing the tracker's remaining open plan labels -- OCII's own Dec 2019 Land Use Map marks this site 'X1' in its gray/non-developable category; this session had previously left X1 with no record after an unrelated street-cluster mislabeling. DataSF Assessor confirms blklot 3806006 as 'Industrial Gov Mixed/Other Use' at this address. Status 'existing' (not touched by Mission Bay's redevelopment, staying as-is) per this project's own convention for pre-existing infrastructure untouched by redevelopment (e.g. UCSF's own Utilities Plant, Pier 70's Building 21).
